en: a General Upaniṣad belonging to the Atharvaveda: I bow to the majesty of the Sun of Consciousness, who has destroyed the enemies that are other than Himself, who delights the wise, who is realized as the Self, and whose form is Sūryanārāyaṇa.

Oṃ. May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O worshipful ones. With firm limbs and bodies, praising you, may we attain that lifespan ordained by the gods. May Indra, of far-reaching fame, grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the all-knowing, grant us well-being; may Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are unharmed, grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us.

Hari Oṃ. Now we shall expound the Sūryātharvāṅgiras. Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi). Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ). Āditya is the deity (devatā). Haṃsaḥ so'ham, conjoined with Agni and Nārāyaṇa, is the seed-syllable (bīja). Hṛllekhā is the power (śakti). Conjoined with the creation beginning with ether (viyat), it is the pin (kīlaka). The application (viniyoga) is for the sake of attaining the fourfold aims of human life (puruṣārtha). With the seed-syllable mounted on the six vowels, one performs the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga) seated upon a red lotus.

He who knows Śrī Sūryanārāyaṇa—the charioteer of the seven horses, golden-hued, four-armed, with two lotuses and hands in the gestures of fearlessness and granting boons, the promulgator of the Kālacakra—he indeed is a Brāhmaṇa.

Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ. Oṃ, we meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our thoughts. Sūrya is the soul of all that moves and stands. Indeed, from Sūrya these beings are born; from Sūrya comes Parjanya, and from Parjanya comes food, which is the self. Homage to you, O Āditya! You alone are the manifest agent of action; you alone are the manifest Brahman; you alone are the manifest Viṣṇu; you alone are the manifest Rudra.

You alone are the Ṛgveda manifest; you alone are the Yajurveda manifest; you alone are the Sāmaveda manifest; you alone are the Atharvaveda manifest; you alone are every Vedic meter manifest. From the Sun, the wind is born; from the Sun, the earth is born; from the Sun, the waters are born; from the Sun, light is born; from the Sun, the sky and the quarters are born; from the Sun, the gods are born; from the Sun, the Vedas are born. Indeed, this Sun is that orb which shines there.

This Āditya is Brahman. Āditya is the internal organs: mind, intellect, consciousness, and ego. Āditya indeed is the vyāna, samāna, udāna, apāna, and prāṇa breaths. Āditya indeed is the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose. Āditya indeed is speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals. Āditya indeed is sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. Āditya indeed is speaking, grasping, moving, excreting, and procreating. Āditya is composed of bliss, composed of wisdom, and composed of knowledge and bliss. *Salutation to Mitra, the radiant one; protect me from death!*

Salutation to the radiant one, the cause of all. From the Sun all beings arise; by the Sun they are protected; into the Sun they attain dissolution. He who is the Sun, he indeed am I. May the divine Savitṛ grant us sight; may Parvata also grant us sight; may Dhātṛ grant us sight. We know the Āditya; we meditate upon the thousand-rayed one. May that Sūrya inspire us. Savitṛ is from behind, Savitṛ is from the front, Savitṛ is from above, and Savitṛ is from below.

May Savitṛ impel us toward complete well-being; may Savitṛ grant us long life. *Oṃ* is the single-syllable Brahman. *Ghṛṇi* consists of two syllables. *Sūrya* consists of two syllables. *Āditya* consists of three syllables. This very Sun has an eight-syllable mantra. He who recites it daily, day after day, truly becomes a Brāhmaṇa; he truly becomes a Brāhmaṇa. Having recited it while facing the Sun, one is liberated from the fear of great diseases; misfortune perishes.

One becomes purified from eating forbidden food; one becomes purified from approaching those who should not be approached; one becomes purified from conversing with the fallen; one becomes purified from conversing with the wicked. At midday, facing the sun, one should recite this. One is immediately liberated from the five great sins (mahāpātaka) just committed. One should not praise this Sāvitrī-vidyā to anyone at all, nor for any reason whatsoever. That fortunate man who recites this in the morning becomes blessed; he acquires cattle and attains the meaning of the Vedas.

Having recited this at the three times of day, one obtains the fruit of a hundred sacrifices. He who recites it when the sun is in his hand crosses over great death—he who knows thus. Thus ends the Upaniṣad.
Hari Oṃ. Peace through the mantra "Bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ."
